text:
rachel: Kicking off a short review of recurring incident patterns for the quarter. I pulled incidents from Jan-Apr and grouped recurring signals. Short list: cache thrash, model hold/unhold churn, deployment memory regressions, noisy retries, and infra config drift.

todd: Thx. Can you share the raw counts and which customers saw most impact?

rachel: Counts (incidents): cache thrash 18, model churn 12, memory reg 9, retry storms 7, config drift 6. Top impacted customers (anonymized): cust-A, cust-C, cust-F.

jing: Are cache thrash incidents correlated with autoscaler policies or client patterns?

rachel: Mostly autoscaler + long-tail sessions that lose KV prefixes. I'll attach a quick correlation chart after this thread.

maya: Proposal: convert recurring signals into three buckets for prioritization: Safety (rollbacks / fail-open), Cost (autoscale inefficiency), Correctness (tokenization / model mismatch). Each bucket gets a lead and a 30-day sprint. Thoughts?

todd: Agree. Suggest Safety gets highest priority. Also propose strict SLAs for rollouts: prefetch + memory sanity checks.

jing: For Cost bucket, we should quantify dollar impact. I can run cost delta per incident for last 90 days.

ops-bot: Note: there are 4 open postmortems tagged recurring-patterns. Please link remediation items to postmortem IDs: PM-2026-0410, PM-2026-0321, PM-2026-0227, PM-2026-0120.

rachel: Action plan draft (owners + due dates):

- Action A: Stabilize KV prefix durability. owner: jing. mitigations: per-customer prefix pin + eviction telemetry + fallback to disk-backed cache. due: 2026-05-20
- Action B: Deployment memory sanity gates. owner: todd. mitigations: add pre-deploy memory simulation + staged rollouts. due: 2026-05-14
- Action C: Autoscale policy rewrite. owner: maya. mitigations: add smoothing window + minimum warm nodes + synthetic loadbench. due: 2026-05-28
- Action D: Retry storm guardrails. owner: rachel. mitigations: server 429 + SDK backoff + alert on retry bursts. due: 2026-05-10
- Action E: Config drift detection. owner: ops-team (rachel backup). mitigations: drift job + signed config manifests. due: 2026-06-01

maya: I can spin up a small Canary plan for the memory gates as part of Action B. Will need test models and an infra quota.

jing: For Action A, question: do we implement disk-backed fallback in the serving runtime or as an intermediate sidecar? Sidecar easier to roll out.

todd: Sidecar first, runtime later if sidecar perf OK. Also prefer feature flag to incrementally enable per-customer.

rachel: Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- KV durability: eviction-related errors reduced by 80% for top 5 customers in 30 days
- Memory gates: <1% rollout-induced OOMs for new model versions
- Autoscale: reduce scale-related latency spikes >2x by 75% in 60 days
- Retry storms: 95% reduction in retry bursts after SDK rollout

jing: I'll run the cost analysis and populate the tracker. ETA EOD Thu.

ops-bot: Reminder: Weekly recurring-patterns summary will post to #incidents every Monday at 09:00 PT if a tracker update exists.

todd: Can we add a brief note to the postmortem template asking teams to tag incidents with "recurring-pattern" if they see a repeat signal? That'll help automation.

rachel: Good call. I'll update the template.

maya: I'll take the Autoscale policy rewrite. Starting RFC next week and will include synthetic workload results.

jing: Linking pre-existing PRs: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/3550 (retry-backoff), https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/3572 (autoscale-tracing).

rachel: I'll create a tracker board column 'recurring-patterns-Q2' and add the actions. Planning checkpoint 2026-05-06.

ops-bot: Checkpoint scheduled: 2026-05-06 16:00 UTC. Participants: rachel, todd, jing, maya.

todd: Thanks all. Short and actionable. If anyone wants to swap owners ping me.

rachel: Closing thread for now. Drop updates in tracker or #incidents.
